label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 12
knowledgePattern: Use interval containment to identify the only possible proper sufficient condition
solution:
Write P for the set of real inputs where the unknown statement is true. A condition is sufficient but not necessary precisely when its input set is a proper subset of P.

Option B, the interval (2,3), is contained in each of A, C, D and E. If any of A, C or D were a proper subset of P, then B would also be a proper subset: every point in B would lie in P, and a point of P outside the larger interval would also lie outside B. Thus none could be the unique answer. E is all real numbers, so it cannot be a proper subset of P.

B can be the unique answer. For example, take P = (3/2,3). B is a proper sufficient subset, while A, C, D and E each include inputs outside P. Answer B.

hints.title: Draw the options on number lines
hints.body: Solve each inequality and mark its interval. For the logarithm option, its input must be positive.
hints.recap: Sufficient means every x allowed by the condition makes P true. Not necessary means other x values can make P true too.
hints.pause: Draw the five sets of allowed x values.

hints.title: Look for one interval inside another
hints.body: Suppose every x in a larger listed interval makes P true. What does that tell you about a smaller listed interval inside it? If P also works outside the larger interval, is that x outside the smaller one too?
hints.recap: Only one option is allowed to be correct.
hints.pitfall: A claim about a larger interval may force a second option to be correct.
hints.pause: Use the intervals inside one another to rule out answers that would not be unique.
